acqinfo.head: Immediate Source of Acquisition
acqinfo.p: Gift of Abbot Low Moffat, 1954; Mrs. E. C. Korten, 1976; and William I. Frothingham, date unknown.
Photographs of Sylvestor and Stephen Pharoah are a gift of W. W. Tooker, 1880.

altformavail.head: Existence and Location of Copies
altformavail.p: Item-level description and digital versions of images from the collection are available for searching via the image database in the library under the object ID prefix V1974.15.
Photographic prints for object IDs V1974.15.3-.11 and V1974.15.15-.16 are also available with this collection.

phystech.head: Physical Characteristics and Technical Requirements
phystech.p: The collection's digital surrogates should be used in place of the originals whenever possible. If a digital surrogate is not available, the corresponding print should be consulted instead of the original glass plate negative.

prefercite.head: Preferred Citation
prefercite.p: Identification of item, date (if known); Brooklyn glass plate negatives collection, V1974.015, Box number, Object ID number; Brooklyn Public Library, Center for Brooklyn History.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: The Brooklyn glass plate negative collection contains 18 items dating from circa 1870 to 1899. The negatives are a mix of anonymous creations, reproductions, and original photography by Henry O. Korten. Images in the collection show rural Brooklyn life, street scenes, snowstorms, and the Brooklyn Navy Yard (formally known as the New York Naval Shipyard) in the late 19th century. Locations featured include the neighborhoods of Flatlands, Fort Greene, Clinton Hill, Brooklyn Heights, as well as Prospect Park and the East River waterfront. Snowstorm scenes located in the Flushing neighborhood of Queens are also included.
Also included in the collection are two portraits of Stephen Taukus "Talkhouse" Pharaoh and Sylvestor Pharoah, circa 1870.

userestrict.head: Conditions Governing Use
userestrict.p: The materials in this collection are in the public domain. While many items at the Center for Brooklyn History are unrestricted, we do not own reproduction rights to all materials. Be aware of the several kinds of rights that might apply: copyright, licensing and trademarks. The researcher assumes all responsibility for copyright questions.

processinfo.head: Processing Information
processinfo.p: The prints of V1974.15.15 and V1974.15.16 (Sylvestor and Stephen Pharoah) were initially added to the Portrait Collection. In 2026, the sitters in the glass plate negatives were identified and subsequently reunited with their photographic prints.
